THESE ARE TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF FAILURE AND THE SECOND IS THE SERIOUS ONE.

The disposition one is a moved value with the test's own instruction attached: it says in its assertion message that this is not a number to update. Read the rest of that message before you touch it — it was written by someone who anticipated exactly this moment and left the reasoning where you would hit it.

The touchstone one is a POSITIVE CONTROL that stopped reproducing. That is not 'a value moved', it is 'the instrument can no longer detect the effect it exists to detect'. A positive control failing means every OTHER assertion in that probe is now unverified — they may be passing because nothing is being measured. Re-pinning it would be the worst available move.

AND A STRUCTURAL GAP THIS EXPOSED, WHICH IS NOT YOURS BUT IS NOW YOUR PROBLEM. scripts/hooks/pre-commit's census guard covers THREE calibration files — calibration.rs, branches_family_calibration.rs, gathering_calibration.rs. disposition_calibration.rs is NOT among them, and it is heavy-tier, so gate-commit never runs it either. So a census refresh can move a value that disposition_calibration pins, and NOTHING between your commit and the chamber's heavy phase will say so. You re-pinned the three files the guard names, correctly and completely; the fourth was invisible from where you were standing.

That gap is worth a decision record or at minimum a board technique post, independent of how you resolve the two tests. It cost you a 1718s chamber run to discover, and the next campaign to refresh a census will pay it again.
